summary: Luffy and his Straw Hat crew sail the Grand Line for the One Piece treasure, exploring islands, fighting pirates and Marines, and defending their friends.

hunger.why: Luffy's bottomless appetite, Sanji's cooking and his rule that no one goes hungry, and feasts after every victory keep food constantly in view.

thirst.why: The crew crosses the Alabasta desert short of water.

feeling-cold-hot.why: Drum Island's snow, the Alabasta desert, and Punk Hazard's fire and ice halves are ordeals of temperature.

sleepiness.why: Luffy and Zoro nap constantly, a running gag.

curiosity.why: Each arc lands the crew on a new island, from Skypiea to Wano, and Luffy's drive to see what lies ahead is the voyage's engine.

explanation-seeking.why: The Void Century, the Poneglyphs, the Will of D, and what the One Piece is are long-running mysteries.

skill-acquisition.why: Luffy develops his Gears, the crew trains for two years, and Zoro pursues mastery of the sword.

play.why: Luffy's games and antics aboard the ship and the crew's horseplay are frequent.

resource-accumulation.why: The One Piece treasure is the goal, Nami hoards gold, and bounties rise.

resource-foraging.why: The crew follows the Log Pose and hunts Poneglyphs, the Road to Laugh Tale, and treasure island by island.

mental-time-travel.why: Each crew member's dream drives them forward, and long backstories reveal the past behind every island.

fear-of-predators.why: Sea Kings, giant beasts, and monstrous creatures attack the ship on the Grand Line.

fear-of-aggressors.why: The crew fights Arlong, Crocodile, Enies Lobby's Marines, Kaido, and countless pirate crews in extended battles.

fear-of-heights.why: The Knock Up Stream to Skypiea and battles high above the ground play on falls.

disgust.why: Occasional gross-out gags and grotesque villains are minor.

pain-aversion.why: Zoro takes Luffy's pain at Thriller Bark, Luffy's Gears damage his body, and battles leave the crew broken and bleeding.

pride.why: Rising bounties, victories over Warlords and Emperors, and Luffy's declarations of becoming Pirate King are recognized achievements.

shame.why: Usopp's shame after leaving the crew is one of the few instances.

moral-pride.why: Zoro says nothing happened after absorbing Luffy's pain, and the crew repeatedly refuses to abandon friends at any cost.

guilt.why: Usopp regrets abandoning the crew, and Luffy blames himself for failing to save Ace.

warmth.why: Shanks's gift of the straw hat, Sanji feeding the starving, and the crew's kindness to strangers set the tone.

moral-blame.why: The crew condemns the World Government's cruelty, and Luffy punches a Celestial Dragon for shooting a friend.

moral-praise.why: Liberated kingdoms such as Alabasta and Dressrosa celebrate the Straw Hats as heroes.

revenge.why: Nami's grudge against Arlong, Law's vendetta against Doflamingo, and Luffy's fury at Kuma drive several arcs.

forgiveness.why: The crew takes Usopp back after his apology, and old enemies become allies.

compassion.why: Luffy frees oppressed islands, Chopper heals the wounded, and the crew protects the weak everywhere.

affiliation.why: Luffy recruits Zoro, Nami, Usopp, Sanji, Chopper, Robin, Franky, Brook, and Jinbe, each after a shared ordeal.

friendship.why: Nakama, the bond of the crew, is the series' creed; Enies Lobby's declaration of war to save Robin is its emblem.

sadness.why: The backstories of Nami, Robin, Chopper, and Brook, the Going Merry's funeral, and Ace's death are deep grief.

humor.why: Luffy's idiocy, Usopp's lies, Sanji's nosebleeds, and constant gags make the series a comedy as much as an adventure.

embarrassment.why: Comic embarrassments are frequent but slight.

reasoning.why: Debate is rare; conflicts are settled by fists.

coalitional-affiliation.why: Pirate crews, the Marines, the Worst Generation alliance, and the Straw Hat Grand Fleet make group loyalty central.

status-seeking.why: Bounties, the titles of Warlord, Emperor, and Pirate King, and Luffy's declaration that he will be king are the series' ladder.

envy.why: Rivals resent Luffy's rise, a minor note.

anger.why: Luffy's rage when friends are hurt, from Arlong Park to Marineford, powers the climactic fights.

hatred.why: Villains like Doflamingo delight in others' suffering, and the crew's foes gloat.

romantic-affiliation.why: Boa Hancock's love for Luffy and Sanji's crushes are comic asides.

sexual-attraction.why: Sanji's nosebleeds and the fan-service drawings of Nami and Robin recur.

long-term-love.why: Oden and Toki's marriage is a rare committed romance.

desire.why: Sanji's lechery is a running gag.

romantic-jealousy.why: Hancock bristles at women near Luffy, played for laughs.

sexual-disgust.why: Absalom's harassment of Nami and similar villainy is briefly disturbing.

parental-care.why: Bellemere dies protecting Nami, Kureha and Hiriluk raise Chopper, and Whitebeard shields his adopted sons.

parental-investment.why: Garp raises Luffy and Ace, and Whitebeard's crew is a family of sons he nurtures.

familial-love.why: The sworn brotherhood of Luffy, Ace, and Sabo, Nami and Bellemere, and Whitebeard's family are among the series' deepest bonds.
